verdict.justification: A provides the more defensible budgeting model by separating the 2025 base rates used for forecasting from current 2026 rates used for validation. B explicitly says its rates “already reflect 2026 carrier actions” but applies another historical-average increase anyway, effectively double-counting escalation in its expected 2026 costs. Both deliverables include the supplied volumes, six-year rate histories, size exclusions, and formula-driven cost comparisons, and they reach the same primary carrier recommendations. A offers more actionable shipping guidance, including UPS cubic-inch bands and a warning that a larger-than-eligible Medium package can reverse the carrier choice. B leaves UPS surcharge treatment unverified and proposes a broad FedEx fallback rather than resolving a material pricing question before issuing operating instructions. Although A is more elaborate, its clearer forecast basis and more precise operational qualifications make it the stronger deliverable.
